F2 (moderate, confirmed): driver docstring misattributes the OFF-arm E1 delta to agent.offline_integration() (zero callers in ree_core); the actual writer is a ContextMemory memory-slot update during SWS/REM replay. secondary_substrate_queue_entries.implementation_hint: e2_fast.py's world_forward head (world_action_encoder + world_transition) is disjoint from predict_next_self (self_action_encoder + self_transition, trained by agent.compute_e2_loss) and its own docstring states it is 'NOT trained as E2's primary objective'. grep over ree_core confirms zero callers of any world_forward-training loss. Add a world_forward loss closure (analogous in shape to compute_e2_loss's predict_next_self MSE) over the EXISTING _world_experience_buffer + _action_experience_buffer (already populated waking-side, ree_core/agent.py ~3129/3154/5865-5871), and wire it into CrossModuleConsolidator.module_losses (or a parallel local-optimizer pass scoped to world_action_encoder/world_transition only, mirroring the existing e1/e2 optimizer-scoping pattern) so it fires during a real sleep cycle. Without this, INV-063 leg B (the V3-EXQ-701b/701c frozen-probe DV over agent.e2.world_forward) cannot register any across-sleep change under any experimental design, no matter how the waking ladder is graded.
